title: Property Binding 🧷
description: Bind component data to HTML element properties using square brackets.

slides.title: Beyond Interpolation: Binding to Properties 🔗
slides.content:
# Property Binding

Interpolation can only put text into the element’s content. Property binding allows you to set the **value of a DOM property** (not an HTML attribute!).

Syntax: `[propertyName]="expression"`

* Examples: `[src]`, `[disabled]`, `[hidden]`, `[class.active]`.
* The expression is evaluated and the property is set to the result.

Interpolation is actually syntactic sugar for property binding on `textContent`.

slides.title: Property Binding vs Interpolation 🤔
slides.content:
Both can display component data, but:

| Feature | Interpolation `{{ }}` | Property Binding `[ ]` |
|---------|-----------------------|------------------------|
| Sets | textContent | Any DOM property |
| Can set boolean? | No | Yes (e.g., `[disabled]`) |
| Can set non‑string? | Only strings | Any data type |

Use property binding for things like `disabled`, `hidden`, `checked`, and when binding to directive inputs.

quizData.question: Which syntax correctly binds the `disabled` property of a button to a component boolean `isDisabled`?
quizData.explanation: Square brackets surround the property name, and the expression inside quotes is evaluated.

slides.title: Binding to Native DOM Properties 🖱️
slides.content:
You can bind to almost any DOM property. Here are common ones:

* `[hidden]` – hides element when true (but still in DOM).
* `[disabled]` – disables button/input.
* `[checked]` – checkbox or radio button.
* `[href]` – for anchor tags.
* `[style.color]` – inline style.
* `[class.active]` – add/remove CSS class.

Angular evaluates the expression and uses the result to set the property.

slides.title: Remember: It's Properties, Not Attributes! ⚠️
slides.content:
HTML attributes are static strings; DOM properties can be any value (boolean, object, etc.).

* `<button disabled="false">` – the button is **still disabled** because the `disabled` **attribute** presence makes it true.
* `<button [disabled]="false">` – the button is **enabled** because you set the DOM property to `false`.

Always use property binding for boolean attributes.

quizData.question: In Angular, `[disabled]="true"` sets the HTML attribute `disabled` to the string 'true'.
quizData.explanation: It sets the DOM property `disabled` to the boolean `true`, not the HTML attribute.
